issue: tód h₂wéseti: expletive subject tód added to impersonal 'it grows bright' (no neuter antecedent); should be bare h₂wéseti

ewewkʷ: no ending, and 3sg-shaped while subject h₁éḱwōs is plural (expect 3pl, e.g. wéwkʷont); kʷnewti lacks the r̥ of kʷr̥néwti 'makes'; wool spelled h₂wlnéh₂m (no laryngeal, no syllabic l̥) and h₂wlh₂néh₂ in the same text; widntbʰós lacks syllabic n̥; ḱḗrd sg + no pronoun for 'our hearts pain us'
tóy-kʷe tetr̥pḗr: plural pronoun and 3pl perfect for the two siblings, between dual h₁dtā́m and dual sísdetām; expect dual tóh₁ + 3du perfect
tóm gʷʰnént 'I slew it': gʷʰnént is 3pl (they slew); 1sg should be gʷʰénm̥
gʷh₂tā́m: 3du ending -tām where the English and the rest of the text need a 2sg imperative (gʷh₂dʰí); also h₂ówins ḱóm: ḱóm used as a postposition taking the accusative for 'beside' is doubtful
older notation without laryngeals or accents (owis, eḱwōs for h₂ówis, h₁éḱwōs); kʷe written as a separate word, not attached as an enclitic (h₁éḱwōskʷe)

kʷékʷloy 'on the wheel' used for 'on the wagon' (the wagon sense would need plural/collective kʷekʷlóh₂ or similar); dʰh₁ént plural after the dual subjects of the surrounding clauses (defensible if all four are meant)
dedwóyth₂e só 'the stranger was afraid': -th₂e is the 2sg perfect ending; 3sg should be dedwóye; also widónt plural for the man and the dog (dual expected)

dʰdʰeh₁dʰí: malformed reduplicated imperative (reduplication has no vowel and the root is full grade); expect dʰédʰh₁dʰi, cf. dédh₃dʰi, or aorist dʰh₁dʰí; also sísdete gʷr̥h₃éte switch to 2pl after a run of 2sg imperatives
tód h₂wést: expletive subject tód added to impersonal 'it grew bright'; should be bare h₂wést (cf. bare h₂wérst in the same text)
h₁wésuh₂ ḱléwos: -uh₂ is neuter plural/collective and does not agree with singular ḱléwos; expect h₁wésu ḱléwos (the formula itself is the classic one)
h₂éwsos léwkt: short-vowel form is the vocative; nominative subject should be h₂éwsōs (as in 052b3ec2, 4a11afaa)
ḱeḱlōts: malformed perfect participle (perfect active participle uses -wos-: ḱeḱluwṓs); mixed notation (tod, owis, aǵrom have no laryngeals or accents, for tód, h₂ówis, h₂éǵrom)
